Formulation  
Valerie, a 29-year-old female, presents with new-onset anxiety symptoms precipitated by starting a stressful new job with a difficult supervisor. Predisposing factors include family history of depression and occasional smoking and alcohol use. Perpetuating factors include poor sleep, avoidance of social and leisure activities, and sustained worry about work performance. Protective factors include strong family support and insight. Anxiety manifests as somatic symptoms including palpitations and panic on awakening, leading to functional impairment but no suicidal ideation. Early intervention with therapy and monitoring is appropriate.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Anxiety disorder related to work stress  
- Patient Goal(s): To reduce anxiety symptoms and feel able to attend work and engage in daily activities without distress  
- Clinical Goal(s): To decrease anxiety severity, improve sleep quality, and enhance coping strategies  
- Actions (Patient): Engage in self-referral for NHS talking therapy, use recommended online resources for anxiety management, monitor symptoms and seek help if worsening  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide referral information and support self-referral to talking therapy; monitor anxiety symptoms and sleep; arrange blood tests to exclude medical causes of palpitations; follow up after blood results  

Secondary Problem: Insomnia related to anxiety  
- Patient Goal(s): To improve sleep quantity and quality  
- Clinical Goal(s): To reduce sleep latency and nocturnal awakenings  
- Actions (Patient): Implement sleep hygiene strategies as advised, avoid caffeine and screen exposure before bed  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide written sleep hygiene advice; review sleep at follow-up; consider further interventions if insomnia persists  

Tertiary Problem: Low mood/depressive symptoms secondary to anxiety  
- Patient Goal(s): To regain enjoyment in activities and improve mood  
- Clinical Goal(s): To reduce depressive symptoms and increase engagement in pleasurable activities  
- Actions (Patient): Attempt gradual re-engagement in hobbies and social activities when able  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Monitor mood symptoms; consider escalation to pharmacotherapy if symptoms worsen or do not improve after therapy  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Anxiety mechanisms, benefits of talking therapy, sleep hygiene, importance of monitoring symptoms  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing anxiety, inability to attend work, panic attacks, worsening sleep, emergence of suicidal thoughts  
- Coping Strategies: Use of online self-help resources; talking therapy engagement; relaxation techniques; seeking social support
